programme: McGarraugh and Baldwin (1971), Lightweight concrete-on-steel composite beams
citations: McGarraugh, J.B. and Baldwin, J.W. Jr. (1971). Lightweight concrete-on-steel composite beams. AISC Engineering Journal 8(3), 90-98 (July 1971).

Companion push-out programme: Ollgaard, J.G., Slutter, R.G. and Fisher, J.W. (1971). Shear strength of stud connectors in lightweight and normal-weight concrete. AISC Engineering Journal 8(2), 55-64 (ref. 4 of the paper; not opened).

screening.decision: included, flagged: lightweight concrete and 36 in slab width

design_space_check.deck_thickness_in: 4.5 (range 4.5-12): in range, at the lower bound
design_space_check.girder_spacing_ft: slab width 36 in = 3.0 ft (range 5-12): 2.0 ft (40 %) below; the Chapman beams in the manuscript use 48 in = 4 ft. Slab width / span = 0.136, inside the database range of spacing/span (5/240 = 0.02 to 12/20 = 0.6)
design_space_check.eta_c: 0.37 plastic, shear-span count with programme push-out strength (range 0.25-1.00): in range
design_space_check.fy_ksi: 36.6 measured static yield point, A36 (range 36-100): in range
design_space_check.loading: monotonic positive bending (short-term test): in scope
design_space_check.concrete: LIGHTWEIGHT, 112 pcf; measured E_c = 2200 ksi against 4250 ksi from the normal-weight ACI expression the database uses, so n = Es/Ec = 13.2 instead of 6.8. Outside the database assumption (normal weight).

screening.very_close_reasoning: Every tabulated design-space parameter is inside the ranges (B2 slab width excepted, handled as for the Chapman beams through the width/span ratio). The only material departure is the lightweight slab. Judged very close for a stiffness-ratio comparison because delta_full and the beam model both use the measured lightweight E_c, so R_meas = delta_full/delta_meas isolates the interface-slip loss; but R_EI(eta_c) was derived at normal-weight modular ratios, and a larger n lowers the composite stiffness gain over the bare steel, so the lightweight beam tests R_EI outside its calibration n. Report it flagged, not pooled silently with normal-weight beams.

concrete.type: E: sanded lightweight (natural sand + rotary-kiln lightweight coarse aggregate, max 3/4 in)

connectors.type: 3/4 in x 3 in headed stud shear connectors (Fig. 1)
connectors.studs_per_group_provenance: NOT stated in the text; the Fig. 1 cross-section shows two studs side by side on the flange. With 2 per group the shear span holds 6 studs, which reproduces the stated "about 50 percent shear connection" under the 1969 AISC allowable-stress rule (V_h = A_s F_y / 2 = 159 kip; q = 13.3 kip for a 3/4 in stud at f'c >= 4 ksi; 6/12 = 0.50). Counting 1 per group would give 25 %, counting all 10 studs of a half-span 83 %; so 2 per group is the only reading consistent with the text.
connectors.layout: 5 groups per half-span, symmetric: 12, 2@22, (28 to load), 18, 24, 12 in to mid-span measured from the beam end (Fig. 1, ST series). 3 groups (6 studs) in each shear span (support to load point) and 2 groups (4 studs) in each half of the constant-moment region; 20 studs in the beam.

strength.provenance: Table 2(a), p. 92: companion push-out specimen P2 (P2 was companion to B2, P3 to B3, etc.); push-out design "identical to that used in the Lehigh phase" (Ollgaard, Slutter and Fisher 1971, ref. 4); push-out geometry not given in this paper
strength.ollgaard_note: 0.5 A_s sqrt(f'c E_c) with the measured E_c (Eq. 2 of the paper, developed at Lehigh); below the A_s F_u cap for F_u >= 56 ksi

stiffness.provenance: digitised push-out curve ("Pushout", solid line) of Fig. 7, journal p. 93 (PDF p. 4); traced by trace_pushout.py
stiffness.caveat: the Fig. 7 push-out curve ends at 23.7 kip/stud at 0.28 in slip, 18 % above the Table 2(a) ultimate of 20 kip at 0.285 in; unresolved (the slip at ultimate agrees). The curve below ~9 kip is hidden under beam-data markers and was not traced.

connectors.beam_derived_connector_data: Fig. 7 also plots stud load-slip derived from strain profiles in the beam for the three shear-span groups (+ exterior, triangle central, circle nearest the load). Text p. 93: B2 initial connector stiffness "essentially the same as the pushout"; for B4 the initial stiffness of the exterior and central groups is lower than the push-out and exterior-stud ultimate only 60 % of push-out. Not digitised (scatter).

digitisation.render: pdftoppm -r 600 -gray (the scan in the PDF is a native 600 ppi CCITT image)
digitisation.method: digitise.py: each grid line (x: 0-7 in every 1 in, labels 0, 2, 4, 6; y: 0-40 kip every 10) fitted as a straight line through 100-400 ink-run centres; points mapped by piecewise-linear interpolation between neighbouring fitted lines ("local", adopted), global affine map reported as a check; markers (filled circles ~33 px) isolated by binary opening (disk r=12), centre = centroid of the erosion core (disk r=12). All 16 plotted markers found, none rejected.
digitisation.verification: overlay_check.py / overlay_check.png: every digitised value re-projected to pixels through the inverse calibration lands on its marker (round-trip residual < 0.02 px); opening centroid vs erosion core differ by <= 0.001 in and <= 0.01 kip; local vs affine calibration differ by up to 0.028 in, 0.09 kip in the elastic points (largest at the first point, where the 0-1 in grid interval is 3 % narrower than the others). The authors' dashed reference lines, fitted through the origin, cross zero load at -0.01 in, which bounds the zero offset.

uncertainty.note: deflection: zero offset +/-0.01 in, calibration +/-0.01 in, marker centring < 0.002 in; the draughting accuracy of the 1971 plotted symbols is unknown and not included

reference_lines_in_figure.check_warning: UNRESOLVED: the authors' dashed "Rigid Connection" and "No Connection" lines do not match a simple elastic calculation for the stated geometry. With W14x30, the measured E_c, span 264 in and loads at 78 in, the transformed-section stiffness is 35.9 kip/in (reaction per in of mid-span deflection) and the no-connection (steel + slab bending) stiffness 15.1 kip/in; the figure lines give 46.9 and 12.9, a ratio of 3.6 against 2.4 computed (the ratio is independent of span and load position). The experimental secant stiffness at the lowest markers (36, 34 kip/in) is close to the computed full-composite value. Possible causes: the figure lines are schematic, or the theory used other section properties. The measured points are unaffected, but the modelling stage should not use the figure's reference lines as a check.

digitisation.method: digitise.py: each grid line (x: 0-7 in every 1 in, labels 0, 2, 4, 6; y: 0-40 kip every 10) fitted as a straight line through 100-400 ink-run centres; points mapped by piecewise-linear interpolation between neighbouring fitted lines ("local", adopted), global affine map reported as a check; markers (filled circles ~33 px) isolated by binary opening (disk r=12), centre = centroid of the erosion core (disk r=12). All 22 plotted markers found, none rejected.
digitisation.verification: overlay_check.py / overlay_check.png: every digitised value re-projected to pixels through the inverse calibration lands on its marker (round-trip residual < 0.02 px); opening centroid vs erosion core differ by <= 0.001 in and <= 0.01 kip; local vs affine calibration differ by up to 0.010 in, 0.20 kip in the elastic points (largest at the first point, where the 0-1 in grid interval is 3 % narrower than the others). The authors' dashed reference lines, fitted through the origin, cross zero load at -0.01 in, which bounds the zero offset.

uncertainty.note: deflection: zero offset +/-0.01 in, calibration +/-0.01 in, marker centring < 0.002 in; the draughting accuracy of the 1971 plotted symbols is unknown and not included

reference_lines_in_figure.check_warning: UNRESOLVED: the authors' dashed "Rigid Connection" and "No Connection" lines do not match a simple elastic calculation for the stated geometry. With W14x30, the measured E_c, span 264 in and loads at 78 in, the transformed-section stiffness is 40.0 kip/in (reaction per in of mid-span deflection) and the no-connection (steel + slab bending) stiffness 15.6 kip/in; the figure lines give 46.0 and 14.3, a ratio of 3.2 against 2.6 computed (the ratio is independent of span and load position). The experimental secant stiffness at the lowest markers (55, 40 kip/in) is close to the computed full-composite value. Possible causes: the figure lines are schematic, or the theory used other section properties. The measured points are unaffected, but the modelling stage should not use the figure's reference lines as a check.
